purpose: Skill-selection cases. `irrelevant` is what makes these measure precision: a system that selects every skill has perfect recall and is useless.

cases.task: Our support assistant forgets the order number a customer gave twenty turns earlier and asks for it again near the end of long chats.
cases.why: State loss across a long conversation is a memory and context-window problem; output formatting, model choice and skill authoring are noise.

cases.task: Move the summarization endpoint onto the newer Claude model tier and stop re-billing the 40k-token system preamble on every request.
cases.why: Stack-conditional: anthropic-claude-api fires only because the detected SDK is Anthropic's — model ids and prompt caching are provider-specific facts that must not be answered from memory.

cases.task: Our research assistant started obeying instructions buried inside web pages users paste in; one page told it to forward the summary to an outside address and it complied.
cases.why: Hard case: 'web pages' plus 'security' pulls toward OWASP web review, but there is no browser injection and no code defect — untrusted content is crossing into the instruction channel.

cases.task: Our payment webhook handler charges some customers twice when the provider redelivers an event after a timeout.
cases.why: Duplicate side effects on redelivery is delivery semantics plus idempotency; auth, caching and contract design are unrelated to the failure.

cases.task: We want customers to export their whole workspace as a zip; exports can take twenty minutes and the team is arguing about whether this belongs in the request path.
cases.why: Long-running work behind a request is an execution-boundary decision; the research and agent-design skills in this loadout have nothing to do with it.

cases.task: Every Monday, pull the week's closed tickets and post a summary to the team channel. Last week the run fired three times and posted duplicates after the API timed out.
cases.why: Hard plus stack-conditional: the recurring-brief framing invites the agent-safety skills, but the real failure is a scheduled job retrying a non-idempotent post, and github-actions fires only because that is the detected scheduler.

cases.task: Rewrite the empty states and error messages in our onboarding flow; right now they say things like 'Error: invalid entity state.'
cases.why: Interface microcopy, not marketing or search content; SEO and positioning would be pure noise on in-product strings.

cases.task: Signups look like they jumped 40% in March. Before we put that in the board deck, confirm whether it is real.
cases.why: Hard case: the obvious read is 'analyze the growth', but a suspicious step-change is a data-quality question first — rule out a tracking or dedupe artifact before interpreting it. postgres fires on the detected warehouse.

cases.task: The nightly job that builds the revenue table silently produced half-empty rows for three days after an upstream column was renamed. It needs to fail loudly and be re-runnable for those dates.
cases.why: A scheduled transform emitting bad rows is pipeline plus data-quality; postgres is a stack negative because the warehouse is Snowflake.

cases.task: We need to split the users.name column into first and last on a 200 million row table without taking the app down, and we need a way back if it goes wrong.
cases.why: Zero-downtime column split on a live table is a staged migration with a verified rollback path; query tuning and access rules are not in play. postgres fires on the detected engine.

cases.task: Users report the settings page shows their old company name for about ten minutes after they change it, then it fixes itself. Only happens in production.
cases.why: Hard case: 'slow to update' reads as a performance or query problem, but a symptom that self-heals on a fixed ten-minute window is a TTL — reproduce it, then look at the cache layer.

cases.task: Preview builds pass but the production deploy lands with the wrong environment variables, and we have no agreed way to back it out.
cases.why: Stack-conditional: vercel-deploy-to-vercel and github-actions fire only because of the detected platform, and docker is wrong for the same reason — there is no container in this delivery path.

cases.task: Before we touch the billing rewrite, find where invoice totals are actually computed and every code path that mutates them.
cases.why: Mapping where behavior lives and how it connects; auditing existing docs and writing new prose are not the ask.

cases.task: Build the team-invite modal from the approved design: email field, role dropdown, and a list of pending invites.
cases.why: Stack-conditional: shadcn-ui and tailwind fire purely on the detected component library and CSS framework; a different UI stack would select neither.

cases.task: Add the resend-verification-email endpoint, and make sure a token can only be redeemed once and expires after an hour.
cases.why: Backend token lifecycle work: the React, Tailwind and browser skills in this loadout must not fire on a stack with no frontend in it.

cases.task: Checkout has been returning 500s for eleven minutes; it started four minutes after last night's release went to full traffic.
cases.why: Hard case: a live outage needs the smallest reversible mitigation first. The deploy correlation tempts a migration-verification detour, but nothing says a migration ran.

cases.task: The admin dashboard takes eight seconds to paint for accounts with more than a thousand projects, and is fine for small accounts.
cases.why: Hard case: 'takes eight seconds to paint' reads as a frontend problem, but cost scaling with row count points at the query layer — measure before touching the bundle.

cases.task: Sales keeps asking for SSO. Work out what we should actually ship first, for whom, and how we will know it worked.
cases.why: Scoping a vague enterprise ask into a first version with success criteria; the marketing and UI-audit skills in this loadout are unrelated.

cases.task: We are on the App Router and want to adopt the new caching model without changing what any page renders.
cases.why: Stack-conditional and hard: the framework adoption skill fires only on the detected Next.js App Router, and 'migration' here is not a database migration.

cases.task: Review the PR that replaces our hand-rolled date parsing with a new npm package that brings in three transitive dependencies.
cases.why: Hard case: 'review' pulls toward general secure-code-review, but the distinguishing risk of this specific change is the new supply-chain surface it adds.

cases.task: Cover the signup-to-first-project flow end to end so it runs in CI on every pull request.
cases.why: Stack-conditional: microsoft-playwright-cli fires only because Playwright is the detected runner; with Cypress the same task should select neither.

cases.task: A bug we fixed in February came back in the last release. Make sure this specific case cannot ship broken again.
cases.why: Hard case: a returning defect needs one pinned regression test, not a new browser-automation suite — and there is no browser anywhere in the stack.

cases.task: Our multi-step signup form works, but people abandon at step three: the steps are long and there is no sense of where you are.
cases.why: Hard case: drop-off at a step is an information-hierarchy and flow problem to audit first; animation polish and code handoff are premature, and the form already exists.

cases.task: Someone committed a .env with live API keys about 200 commits back. The file was deleted in a later commit but it is still in history.
cases.why: Hard case: it looks like history surgery, but the governing skill is credential handling and rotation. 'rollback' is about reverting a release, not rewriting history, and nothing here is a defect hunt.
